text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The foreign ministers of Vietnam and the Philippines have called for greater efforts to develop ties in areas including security and defence.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet wants closer cooperation between northeast provinces and the neighbouring Chinese authorities on Hainan island, particularly in the sharing of sea transport routes.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for the development of the bicycle and electric fan industries as part of efforts to promote made in Vietnam products.
-- The politburo has called for party members and members of the public to participate in efforts to improve education and develop science and technology.
-- Vietnam and the Philippines have agreed to prepare for a second joint sea study at the earliest possible date.
-- The Vietnam General Coal Corporation expects 9.3-9.6 million tonnes of coal to be produced during 1997, of which 3.7-3.9 million tonnes will be exported.
-- The authorities are maintaining a ban on the use of firecrackers and fireworks ahead of this year's Traditional Tet Lunar New Year.
-- Hanoi's Party Committee has asked party cells to practise thrift in celebrations for the 67th anniversary of the Communist Party and the Lunar New Year Festival.

-- The Ho Chi Minh City People's Council begins a meeting today to review the socio-economic, security and national defence situations, and work out development plans for 1997 and for the next five years.
-- Ho Chi Minh City is to set up a board to prepare for the city's 300th-anniversary in 1998.
